title: The procurement question
text: Welcome to Windward, a pilot for a UK energy procurement team. Before buying tomorrow's electricity, the team needs to understand expected wind generation and how much that forecast could miss. This portal brings those two questions together, using only Elexon national wind actuals and forecasts. We are reviewing historical decisions in January 2026.

title: The decision-time view
text: The first screen reconstructs what was available when the purchase decision was made. Our explicit pilot cutoff is ten a.m. London time on the preceding day. It is configurable, because the challenge does not define a precise cutoff. January decision dates correspond to deliveries from the second of January through the first of February.

title: Four numbers that matter
text: The latest selected interval forecasts five thousand and seven megawatts of wind. Across the month, the typical absolute miss is approximately two thousand and sixteen megawatts. The root mean square error is larger because it gives greater weight to severe misses. Positive bias shows that wind was over-predicted on average, which can expose a buyer to a shortfall.

title: Compare the forecast with reality
text: The main chart compares delivered wind in green with the dashed day-ahead forecast. Hovering reveals generation, error, publication time and the decision cutoff. The separation between the lines makes sustained misses visible. Elexon's forecast targets in this extract are hourly, so the hourly value is explicitly held across two half-hours and labelled throughout the product.

title: See direction and magnitude
text: The error chart shows forecast minus actual, with a clear zero line. Amber above zero means less wind arrived than the forecast suggested. Green below zero means more wind arrived than anticipated. The procurement lens summarizes historical bias and the ninetieth percentile of absolute error. That percentile describes this sample; it is not a promise about future outcomes.

title: Focus the analysis
text: Let's narrow the analysis to one day. The same shared filters update the chart, matched interval count, all accuracy metrics and the export. Decision settings let the team explore a different cutoff or delivery hour range. A separate delivery-date mode supports a January delivery review without silently changing the meaning of the original January decision requirement.

title: Quantify reliability
text: Accuracy analysis explains every metric beside its value. Mean absolute error describes a typical miss; root mean square error highlights larger misses. MAPE expresses percentage error but can be unstable at low output. WAPE provides a volume-weighted alternative. Bias gives direction, and the maximum error identifies the largest individual miss. Missing pairs never count as zero errors.

title: Find the periods to investigate
text: Daily mean absolute error identifies difficult delivery days. The time-of-day chart reveals recurring patterns across half-hours, while the distribution shows how often over-forecast and under-forecast errors reached different magnitudes. These views help the team focus its investigation. They do not claim a financial-risk model or determine purchase volumes without the utility's demand and contracted supply.

title: Trace every delivery interval
text: Forecast analysis makes every interval traceable. The table includes the selected publication, forecast, actual, signed error, absolute error and percentage error. It can be searched, sorted and paginated. The alignment label identifies hourly holds. Export CSV downloads the entire filtered selection, rather than only the current table page, so the analyst can review the evidence outside the portal.

title: A transparent pilot
text: The methodology view documents sources, selection rules, formulas and source health. The bundled real Elexon extract provides complete paired coverage for the default January decision view. Refresh retrieves new source records and preserves the existing dataset if Elexon is unavailable. The business value is clear visibility into forecast availability and historical uncertainty, with assumptions the team can inspect and change.

title: Architecture and responsibility
text: For the technical review, the architecture has four clear responsibilities. React renders the product and sends a shared filter contract. FastAPI validates requests and returns typed analysis. Pure Python analytics select eligible forecast vintages and calculate metrics. The repository and Elexon adapter handle source validation, caching and network requests. Business calculations and procurement observations are owned by the backend.

title: The critical selection invariant
text: The central invariant is that a forecast publication must be no later than the historical decision cutoff. The code computes the preceding local calendar day, converts the cutoff to UTC, then chooses the greatest eligible publication time. Publications one second after cutoff and publications on delivery day are excluded. Delivery, publication, cutoff and source target remain separate fields in the comparison response.

title: Alignment and data validation
text: The pipeline generates expected half-hour slots independently of the source records. It validates timezone-aware grid timestamps and finite non-negative generation, filters actuals to WIND, deduplicates identical vintages, and quarantines conflicts. An hourly publication may supply the second half-hour of its own hour only. Missing actuals stay null. Revised actuals use the latest retrieved publication and that limitation is documented.

title: Metrics and missing data
text: The metric function uses matched pairs only. Error is forecast minus actual; mean error is also the bias. MAE averages absolute errors, while RMSE averages squared errors before taking the square root. MAPE excludes zero actuals and reports their count. WAPE is undefined when total actual is zero. Empty comparisons return null metrics. Daily and intraday summaries reuse the same function.

title: Reliable upstream integration
text: The sole upstream adapter calls the FUELHH and WINDFOR stream endpoints using publication windows. Three-day chunks, four concurrent requests, finite timeouts and bounded retries keep the integration predictable. December publications support the first January deliveries; February actual publications cover the final January decision. A genuine source snapshot, retrieval metadata and a SHA two fifty-six manifest make the demonstration reproducible.

title: Caching, refresh and safety
text: Ordinary reads use the newest valid persisted cache or bundled snapshot. Manual refresh is single-flight within a process and validates the new extract before replacement. Atomic writes protect the cache; a failed or materially truncated refresh preserves the previous data. Public refresh requests require a server-configured token. The UI reports retrieval age, source-quality issues and safe errors without exposing Python stack traces.

title: Frontend and REST contract
text: The frontend is split into reusable shell, filters, KPIs, charts, table, states and four focused views. An abortable hook prevents superseded requests from overwriting new filters. The API exposes health, configuration, dashboard, actuals, selected forecasts, comparison, accuracy, summary, export and protected refresh. OpenAPI documentation is available on the Python service. Relative API URLs keep production communication on one origin.

title: Testing the business boundary
text: Tests cover cutoff inclusivity, hindsight exclusion, hourly alignment, missing values, zero denominators, known metric values, January boundaries, duplicates, revised actuals and cache failure recovery. API integration tests run against the real bundled snapshot without network access. Browser checks exercise real frontend-to-backend filters, exports, table interactions, mobile navigation and automated accessibility. Test results and screenshots are included as local verification evidence.

title: Docker and deployment
text: Docker Compose defines an unprivileged Python API and an unprivileged Nginx frontend, with a health check and persisted cache volume. Vercel configuration packages the Python entrypoint, React build and historical snapshot on one origin. Docker execution could not be verified because the engine is absent here. Public GitHub publication, Vercel deployment and unlisted YouTube upload still require the owner's authenticated account access.

title: Tradeoffs and handover
text: This is a focused pilot designed for the sixteen-hour challenge. It deliberately uses no unrelated business datasets or distributed infrastructure. Serverless caches are instance-local, the cutoff and hourly hold are explicit assumptions, and historical errors are not future confidence guarantees. The README, technical documentation, setup commands, demo script and requirement audit support review and handover. Public links must be verified signed out before submission.
